claim_ceiling: This file defines proposed acceptance targets. It contains no measured benchmark results and does not qualify any runtime, device or physical safety property.

benchmarks.workload: The committed home-effect conformance corpus v1.
benchmarks.method: Load the schema and corpus, reject malformed/duplicate trace IDs and step IDs, evaluate every snapshot against the reference model, and count evaluated snapshots.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every test invocation; record corpus version and source SHA.

benchmarks.workload: Every committed adversarial vector plus all newly added vectors.
benchmarks.method: Compare the full typed decision, including denial reason, not only allow/deny.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every test invocation, including the positive control.

benchmarks.workload: At least the critical mutants enumerated in this plan: ignore revocation, accept stale adapter admission, skip lease/journal/postcondition guard, bypass role binding, allow changed request fingerprints, allow empty/whitespace request fingerprints, and redispatch ambiguous outcomes.
benchmarks.method: Introduce one narrowly scoped fault in the relevant enforcement predicate at a time; verify a named test kills each mutant. A mutant that cannot be exercised is not counted as killed.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every release candidate and any change to effect authorization/retry/reconciliation code.

benchmarks.workload: The Cartesian product of six gate booleans, four risk classes, seven journal states, three binding cases, four journal identity cases, two expiry states, three attempt limits and three attempt counts.
benchmarks.method: Enumerate 64 × 4 × 7 × 3 × 4 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 387072 deterministic input combinations. For every AllowDispatch outcome, assert current authority/admission, exact binding, lease, durable journal, observer, risk stop, freshness, retry budget and consistent journal state. For unresolved or terminal journal states, assert that AllowDispatch is impossible.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Run on every Rust test invocation. Extend with temporal sequence generation and a finite-state model checker before making claims about arbitrary event histories.
evidence_required: Declared Cartesian dimensions and evaluated combination count
Counterexample inputs retained as regression fixtures if any

benchmarks.workload: Every supported corpus vector executed by both Luminous and the actual Mycelix Hearth 004E edge path.
benchmarks.method: Compare decisions keyed by corpus version, trace ID and step ID; unsupported and unevaluable vectors fail closed and cannot count as passes.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Required when either repository changes authority, admission, physical executor, journal/recovery, compensation, provider dispatch or outcome reconciliation.

benchmarks.workload: Reference Raspberry Pi 5 and one documented low-power x86-64 host; warmed process; 1 KB and 16 KB representative inputs; 100 decisions/second; no network in the measured decision function.
benchmarks.method: Report p50/p95/p99, CPU model, OS, compiler mode, input size and request count. Benchmark the production runtime gate separately when it exists; do not substitute the pure reference model.
benchmarks.sample_plan: At least 30 batches per host and input size, with raw timing samples retained.

benchmarks.workload: The actual durable journal on a documented SSD-backed reference host, with sync semantics enabled.
benchmarks.method: Measure the end-to-end durable commit boundary under normal and bounded concurrent load. Never relax fsync/durability guarantees to meet a timing target.
benchmarks.sample_plan: At least 10000 journal commits per host/storage profile; report tail latency and errors.

benchmarks.workload: Crash injection before journal commit, after dispatch intent, immediately after provider call, after provider acknowledgement, after observed postcondition, and before terminal journal commit.
benchmarks.method: At each failpoint restart the executor; assert unresolved attempts enter reconciliation only, and count physical/provider dispatch invocations using an instrumented test adapter.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every failpoint and provider profile; repeat each failpoint at least 100 times once an executable runtime harness exists.

benchmarks.workload: A named essential-local-service inventory during a 24-hour network partition, including loss of internet, remote identity and optional inference.
benchmarks.method: Probe every defined essential operation on a fixed cadence; separately verify that cloud-dependent/authority-sensitive new effects fail closed when freshness cannot be established.
benchmarks.sample_plan: At least one full 24-hour run per supported host profile and each declared degradation mode.

benchmarks.workload: Restore a documented household configuration and encrypted backup onto a clean test installation with secrets provisioned through the documented local process.
benchmarks.method: Time from declared recovery start to owner-verifiable service availability; verify checksums and actual configuration/data completeness, not merely successful process start.
benchmarks.sample_plan: At least 10 clean-room restores across supported release updates.

benchmarks.workload: Acknowledged household configuration changes before a forced host/storage failure.
benchmarks.method: Inject faults at defined points, restore from the documented backup/journal strategy, and measure lost acknowledged configuration against a timestamped test log.
benchmarks.sample_plan: At least 10 fault-injected restore cycles per storage strategy.

benchmarks.workload: Evidence manifests, CI logs, trace outputs, exported diagnostics and public artifacts containing seeded secret markers, household names, stable entity identifiers and synthetic occupancy traces.
benchmarks.method: Inject unique markers into each sensitive field class and scan all public/shareable outputs; verify expected local-only evidence still remains available for diagnosis.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every release candidate and every change to logging, evidence export, telemetry or CI artifacts.

benchmarks.workload: Every data class advertised as exportable in the product's portability manifest, excluding secrets that must be re-provisioned rather than copied.
benchmarks.method: Export, import on a clean test instance, compare canonical manifests and verify the owner can inspect the result without a vendor cloud account.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every supported upgrade/migration path and release format version.

benchmarks.workload: Declared update failure modes: interrupted download, invalid signature, failed health check and interrupted activation.
benchmarks.method: Inject each failure against a disposable test system; confirm return to a previously verified bootable service state and verify journal/data integrity.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every supported update mechanism and boot layout; at least 20 repeats per failure mode before hardware qualification.

benchmarks.workload: All 1,000,000 length-six histories over a ten-event alphabet: attempt/retry, household-authority revocation, adapter drift, admission revalidation, lease loss, crash/restart, late provider acknowledgement, definitive no-effect observation, reconciled success, and time advancement.
benchmarks.method: Enumerate the complete finite set of length-six event strings. Reset the synthetic household to a clean initial state for every history; replay events; evaluate each attempt through the reference gate; assert no dispatch from an unresolved/terminal journal state, no dispatch with revoked authority/stale admission/missing lease/expired request, and no attempt-budget or modeled-journal-count violation. Preserve any counterexample as a named regression trace.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Run in the Rust test suite on each candidate. This is exhaustive only for the declared event alphabet and history length; expand history length or use a finite-state model checker before making unbounded temporal claims.

benchmarks.workload: Protocol-model and runtime vectors send state_changed frames with correct, stale, unknown and mismatched subscription IDs across authentication, subscription acknowledgement, bootstrap, live and reconnect phases.
benchmarks.method: Require exact active subscription-ID matching before buffering or forwarding any event. Wrong IDs fail closed; stale connection epochs cannot advance the active session. Track every accepted/buffered/delivered event and preserve mismatches as regression vectors.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every protocol conformance run; runtime promotion additionally exercises the exact decoded Home Assistant frame path and records source SHA, corpus version and transport build identity.
evidence_required: Per-frame subscription and session epoch decision log
Mutant proving mismatched subscription ID is rejected

benchmarks.workload: At least 10,000 deterministic event interleavings around native subscribe_entities acknowledgement, initial compact snapshot, incremental add/change/remove frames, application acknowledgement, and reconnect epoch change.
benchmarks.method: Prefer Home Assistant's native subscribe_entities stream, restricting entity_ids to the exact validated profile allowlist. Validate the subscription ID; apply its initial compact snapshot before processing later deltas on the same serialized receive loop; apply additions, field-level changes/removals and entity removals only for allowlisted IDs. For any future provider that exposes separate snapshot and event subscriptions, require subscribe-first plus buffered replay. Compare final projection against an ordered event oracle and retain counterexamples.
benchmarks.sample_plan: Every release candidate for the native read-only transport and any change to snapshot/bootstrap/reconnect sequencing. Synthetic model results and real transport results are reported separately.
evidence_required: Exact source and transport build SHAs
Initial snapshot and ordered event-oracle digests
Evidence class distinguishing synthetic from live transport
